content.text: No minimum commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall, or volume floor exists anywhere in the agreement. Fees are tied to the Fee Schedule for the licence granted and maintenance actually taken, maintenance runs on a renewable one-year term, and we hold a 90-day termination-at-will right.

input.quote: (a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge or volume floor on Sparkling: searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" return nothing relevant (the only "commitment" hit, p0143, is the no-agency clause). Section 11 (p0084) simply requires payment of the fees set out in the Fee Schedule for the licence and services actually taken; Section 2 (p0028) charges additional fees only if Sparkling elects to use the Software beyond the Authorized Locations; and maintenance under Section 10 (p0065) runs on a "renewable one-year term" rather than a multi-year committed spend. Sparkling also holds an unconditional right to terminate on ninety (90) days' notice (p0118), so there is no locked-in commitment even at the fee level. The Section 3 restrictions are ordinary licence-scope limits, not volume caps operating as a purchase floor. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage or ordered services only), so no redline is warranted.
